narr: A late-season trough during the monsoon, just off the southern US coast, promoted deep southerly flow from the surface through mid levels of the troposphere. This in combination with a moisture axis extending up from Sonora and marginal afternoon instability promoted the development of isolated thunderstorms across southeast California and southwest Arizona. With just enough speed shear, a few storms trained or redeveloped over the same areas resulting in localized flooding impacts with average rainfall rates around 1 inch per hour. An isolated strong to severe storm near Desert Center produced radar estimated rainfall near 2 inches in 1 hour, leading to flash flooding.
ev: Local law enforcement reported road closures in several locations due to flash flooding. This included State Route 177, which was closed between Ragsdale Road and State Route 62. Closures reported at 1755PDT. Timing adjusted based on radar estimated rainfall. No damages or injuries were reported.
